name: Persian royal courier, Susa to Sardis
what: Darius's relay riders, a fresh horse at each station, covered the 2,700 km Royal Road in about nine days; a walker took about 90.

name: Death of Nero reaches Galba
what: Galba's freedman Icelus rode from Rome to Clunia in Spain in seven days with the news that Nero was dead.

sources.cite: Ramsay, A. M. (1925). The speed of the Roman imperial post. Journal of Roman Studies 15, 60-74.

name: Fall of Constantinople reaches Venice
what: Constantinople fell on 29 May 1453; the news reached Venice about a month later, by ship via Crete.

sources.cite: Runciman, S. (1965). The Fall of Constantinople 1453. Cambridge.

name: Victory at Trafalgar reaches London
what: Battle on 21 October; Lieutenant Lapenotière landed at Falmouth on 4 November and reached the Admiralty on 6 November after 37 hours and 21 changes of horses.

name: Treaty of Ghent reaches New York
what: Peace was signed on 24 December 1814; the news reached New York on 11 February 1815, after the Battle of New Orleans had been fought.

sources.cite: Hickey, D. R. (1989). The War of 1812: A Forgotten Conflict. University of Illinois Press.

name: Victory at Waterloo reaches London
what: Wellington's dispatch, carried by Major Henry Percy, reached London on the night of 21 June, three days after the battle.

name: Letter from Calcutta to London (1820 average)
what: Around the Cape by sail, a message from Calcutta took on average 154 days to reach London.

sources.cite: Kaukiainen, Y. (2001). Shrinking the world. European Review of Economic History 5, 1-28.

name: Letter from Calcutta to London (1860 average)
what: Steamers and the overland route through Egypt cut the average to 39 days.

sources.cite: Kaukiainen, Y. (2001). Shrinking the world. European Review of Economic History 5, 1-28.

name: Pony Express, Missouri to California
what: Relays of riders cut east-west mail to about 10 days; the transcontinental telegraph put it out of business in October 1861.

name: Lincoln's assassination reaches London
what: Lincoln was shot on 14 April 1865; with no working Atlantic cable, the news arrived by steamer and was in London on 26 April.

name: Atlantic cable: London to New York the same day
what: From 27 July 1866 the transatlantic cable carried messages in minutes; news between London and New York now arrived the same day.

notes.-480: Persian royal courier: about 2,700 km in 9 days (Herodotus).
notes.68: Roman courier Icelus: Rome to Clunia, about 1,900 km by road, in 7 days (Plutarch).
notes.1250: Mongol yam riders: 200-300 km a day.
notes.1500: Inca chasqui runners: up to about 300 km a day.
notes.1805: Lapenotière with Trafalgar dispatches: 271 miles in 37 hours of hard riding by post-chaise.

sources.cite: Kaukiainen, Y. (2001). Shrinking the world. European Review of Economic History 5, 1-28.
